title: Chicken Katsu Curry
kicker: A panko-cutlet the size of your ambition, drowned in sweet Japanese curry. Sleep well after.
story: Katsu curry is the best of two imports: British-introduced curry powder turned Japanese over a century into thick, sweet, gently spiced sauce, and the Viennese schnitzel transplanted into panko-fried tonkatsu. Put them on rice together and you get Japan's favorite comfort plate — crunch against silk, rich against sweet.

The curry roux is worth making from scratch: butter and flour cooked dark, curry powder, garam masala, grated apple and a square of dark chocolate for depth. It takes twenty minutes and tastes like the expensive version of the block-shaped shortcuts — which, to be fair, are also good and fully respectable on a Tuesday.
fun_fact: Japanese curry (karē) came via the Royal Navy, which adopted curry from the British. It is now so domesticated that it is considered a national dish — served weekly in a third of Japanese school cafeterias.

ingredients.note: S&B style if you can find it

steps.title: The roux
steps.text: Melt butter, cook onion until translucent. Add flour and cook, stirring, 3 minutes until it smells like shortbread. Add both spice powders and cook 30 seconds more — blooming the spices in fat is the difference between curry that tastes boiled and curry that tastes cooked.

steps.title: Loosen and enrich
steps.text: Whisk in stock gradually — lumps are just future gravy, whisk them out. Add carrots, apple, soy, chocolate. Simmer 20 minutes until thick enough to plate in a wave. Taste: it should be gently sweet, warm, not spicy-forward.

steps.title: Bread the cutlets
steps.text: Flour, egg, panko — press the crumbs on firmly. Chill 10 minutes; the breading hydrates and grips better.

steps.title: Fry with confidence
steps.text: Oil at 170°C / 340°F, medium-high. Fry 3-4 minutes per side to deep gold. Rest on a rack, never paper — trapped steam is the enemy of crunch. Slice across into strips so it fans over the rice.

steps.title: Plate the classic way
steps.text: Rice on one side, cutlet fanned over it, curry sauce ladled along the border — not over the whole cutlet, or the crunch dies. Shredded cabbage on the side, tonkatsu sauce for dipping if you have it.

notes: Panko vs. breadcrumbs is not close: panko's large flakes fry into shatter. Do not substitute.
The sauce freezes well for a month — double the batch, thank yourself later.
Air-fryer cutlets: 200°C / 400°F for 12 minutes, flipped once, sprayed with oil. Respectable crunch.
